about.heroSubtitle: We envision Ottawa as a global leader in responsible AI innovation, where technology advances the public good and empowers every community.
about.missionBody1: ORAH seeks to drive the future of ethical AI through education, advocacy, and cross-sector collaboration to advance transparency, accountability, and policy, while uniting a community committed to responsible AI solutions and practices.
about.missionBody2: Our goal is to inspire and support the creation of <count>500 responsible tech innovations</count> in Ottawa over the next 10 years, building a thriving ecosystem where AI serves humanity with <values>transparency, fairness, and integrity</values>.
about.storyBody1: AI is transforming innovation across sectors and everyday life but presents a pressing challenge in ethics, governance, privacy, and data protection. As adoption accelerates, embedding responsibility into AI development is no longer optional — it is essential to protect against potential harm while unlocking its full benefits.
about.storyBody2: The Ottawa Responsible AI Hub (ORAH), a non-profit initiative, provides a platform to advance dialogue, education, advocacy, and collaboration on responsible AI. By bringing together professionals, policymakers, researchers, civil society, and the public, ORAH is uniquely positioned to lead this movement and build a community committed to responsible AI.
about.quoteText: "Digital inclusion is no longer only about internet access. It is about helping people feel confident participating in a world that is changing fast. That is exactly what ORAH is built to do."
about.ottawaBody: Ottawa is Canada's tech hub, home to over 1,700 technology companies, research institutions, and policy think tanks. The city's proximity to federal government bodies and institutions like the National Research Council (NRC), Shopify, and the University of Ottawa's AI + Society Initiative positions it uniquely to lead in responsible AI and digital ethics.
about.ctaBody: Be part of shaping the future of ethical AI in Ottawa and beyond. Connect with professionals, researchers, and advocates who share your values.

programs.title: Our Initiatives
programs.subtitle: At the Ottawa Responsible AI Hub (ORAH), we believe ethical AI should be inclusive, transparent, and accessible to all. Our flagship initiatives reflect that mission.

toc.heroSubtitle: We believe that by fostering inclusive collaboration, ethical innovation practices, and community engagement, we can accelerate the development of responsible AI solutions that advance public good in Ottawa and beyond.
toc.modelSubtitle: A strategic logic model connecting what we invest to the long-term change we seek.
toc.principle1: At the Ottawa Responsible AI Hub, we are grounded in the belief that artificial intelligence must be developed and governed in ways that uphold the rights, values, and wellbeing of all people in our city, our country, and our world.
toc.principle2: We are committed to fostering a future where AI systems are transparent, inclusive, equitable, and trustworthy, reflecting the democratic principles, diversity, and spirit of innovation that define both Ottawa and Canada as a whole.
toc.principle3: Through collaboration, education, research, and advocacy, the Ottawa Responsible AI Hub seeks to ensure that AI technologies serve the public good, enhance social trust, and strengthen the communities we call home.
toc.principleQuote: "AI must be governed with intention, built with care, and deployed for the benefit of all."
toc.commitmentsSubtitle: Five principles that guide every initiative, partnership, and conversation at ORAH.
toc.finalTitle: AI must be governed with intention, built with care, and deployed for the benefit of all.
toc.finalBody: This principle guides our every action, conversation, and collaboration, ensuring that Ottawa leads by example in building a future where technology empowers all people.

seniors.tagline: Learn AI. Build confidence. Stay in control.
seniors.hero1: Imagine being told the world has changed, but no one stops to show you how. For many older adults, AI is not a tool yet. It is a source of anxiety. And that is not their fault.
seniors.hero2: This July, ORAH is delivering AI for All: Empowering Seniors in Ottawa: a six-week community program helping adults build confidence with AI in a practical, supportive, and fully accessible environment.
seniors.noTechRequired: No tech background required. Just curiosity and conversation.
seniors.heroImageFunded: Funded by the Government of Canada 🇨🇦
seniors.detailAccessValue: Fully Accessible · No prior experience needed
seniors.aboutBody1: AI for All: Empowering Seniors is a funded community initiative led by the Ottawa Responsible AI Hub (ORAH). The program delivers a six-session AI literacy workshop series for adults, using an intergenerational co-facilitation model in which trained Youth Partners support seniors through hands-on, personalized learning.
seniors.aboutBody2: It operates as a pilot (Cohort 1) from July to August 2026, with documentation and evaluation designed to inform a potential Year 2 national scale-up.
seniors.aboutBody3: Digital inclusion is no longer only about internet access. It is about helping people feel confident participating in a world that is changing fast. That is exactly what this program is built to do.
seniors.why1: Seniors are among the fastest-growing demographic groups in Canada and among the most underserved when it comes to AI education.
seniors.why2: AI-enabled scams, misinformation, and fraud disproportionately affect older adults who have not had access to practical digital literacy support.
seniors.why3: Many seniors are being asked to engage with AI-assisted healthcare portals, government services, and communication tools without any preparation.
seniors.why4: This program is designed to close that gap, one community and one conversation at a time.
seniors.fundedFull: Funded by the Government of Canada 🇨🇦, New Horizons for Seniors Program (NHSP)
seniors.sessionsSubtitle: Across five sessions running July 16 to August 14, you will explore AI and its role in everyday life: from staying safe online to how AI is used in healthcare, communication, and daily routines. Every session is welcoming, practical, and paced for participants with no prior technology experience.
seniors.sessionFooter: Sessions 1–4 run weekly on Thursdays · 2 hours each · Sessions 1–4 at RRCRC · Closing celebration on Friday, August 14
seniors.s1Desc: An accessible, plain-language introduction to artificial intelligence, covering what it is, how it works, and where participants already encounter it in their daily lives.
seniors.s1h1: Icebreaker: "AI in my day?" Share a technology you used this week
seniors.s1h2: Plain-language overview: what AI is and isn't, with everyday examples
seniors.s1h3: Paired activity with your Youth Volunteer: spot AI in your home
seniors.s1h4: Group discussion and pre-programme confidence survey
seniors.s2Desc: Practical guidance on protecting yourself online: recognising scams, understanding deepfakes, and knowing how your personal information is used by AI-powered tools.
seniors.s2h1: Real-world scenarios: AI phone scams and fake voice messages
seniors.s2h2: Hands-on privacy settings walk-through with your Youth Volunteer
seniors.s2h3: Safe habits: no personal data in AI chats, verify before you trust
seniors.s3Desc: Explore AI in daily activities and learn how it is used in healthcare and wellness. Understand what to watch for and how to make informed decisions on your own terms.
seniors.s3h1: Try an everyday AI tool (maps, voice assistant, weather app) with support
seniors.s3h2: AI for health: medication reminders, symptom checkers, and telehealth
seniors.s3h3: Discussion: "Would you trust AI with your health?"
seniors.s3h4: Key message: AI supports your health. It does not replace your doctor
seniors.s4Desc: Discover how AI-powered tools can help you stay in touch with family, friends, and your community, safely and with confidence.
seniors.s4h1: Video calls, translation tools, and AI writing assistants
seniors.s4h2: Hands-on: draft a message to a friend or family member using AI
seniors.s4h3: Discussion: can AI help reduce loneliness? What does it miss?
seniors.s4h4: Preview of the closing celebration session
seniors.s5Desc: A hands-on practice session, an intergenerational panel discussion, and a closing celebration. You leave with tools, confidence, and a community to keep exploring.
seniors.s5h1: Open Lab: explore any AI tool you've discovered, at your own pace
seniors.s5h2: Community Showcase: pairs share their highlights from the programme
seniors.s5h3: Intergenerational Panel: "AI, Work, and Us", moderated by Ugo Okoye
seniors.s5h4: Youth Volunteer recognition and programme closing by Somto Mbelu
seniors.teamSubtitle: Our sessions are led by experienced AI educators and supported by trained Youth Partners who bring both knowledge and energy to every workshop. Every facilitator is committed to making AI education accessible, welcoming, and grounded in responsible AI principles.
seniors.detailsConfirmed: Details will be shared once confirmed.
seniors.leadFacilitatorDesc: Our lead facilitator brings expertise in AI education and community engagement. Details will be shared once confirmed.
seniors.youthPartnersBody: Each workshop session is co-facilitated by trained Youth Partners: young people who bring technical knowledge, patience, and a genuine enthusiasm for helping older adults feel at ease with new technology. Youth Partners provide one-on-one support throughout every session, creating an intergenerational learning environment built on mutual respect.
seniors.ctaBody: Registration is open for adults in Ottawa. Spaces are limited, so secure your spot today.
seniors.volunteerTitle: Know a young person who wants to make a difference?
seniors.volunteerBody: We are looking for enthusiastic high school and university students to join our team as Youth Partner volunteers. No prior tech experience needed. Just bring curiosity and a willingness to learn alongside our participants.
seniors.closingQuote: Digital inclusion is no longer only about internet access. It is about helping people feel confident participating in a world that is changing fast. That is exactly what this program is built to do.
